candidate.scope: The assigned Illumina NOMe-Seq schematic (Nucleosome Occupancy and Methylome Sequencing; primary-paper spelling NOMe-seq): native chromatin accessibility is written as GpC methylation and read together with native CpG methylation by bisulfite sequencing. The final Control and M.CviPI rows are retained as separate reference and treated readouts under one assay target. The left title icon is descriptive. M.CviPI and BS-Seq are components, not additional method targets. This is a schematic-level genome-wide architecture, not one fully specified library implementation: the combined Bisulfite conversion BS-Seq caption is resolved into conversion and sequencing for each row, without assigning adapter timing or kit-specific internals. The 2012 and 2016 papers support this shared architecture but describe different complete preparations. Unshown locus-specific cloning, MPE-seq and other cited assays are outside the target scope.

states.label: M.CviPI BS-Seq readout
features: The final M.CviPI row has added red marks on exposed DNA, with open circles over gray protected intervals. These are explanatory methylation/accessibility symbols rather than literal nucleotide letters or retained nucleosomes.

Native CpG methylation and introduced GpC accessibility are read together on the same genomic strand/fragment. A GpC methylation gap signifies inaccessibility, consistent with nucleosomes or other tight binding proteins.

The four figure annotations across the two rows are Protected methylated, Unprotected methylated, Protected unmethylated and Unprotected unmethylated. Primary Figure 1A resolves the methylated/unmethylated axis as endogenous CpG status; protection is the separate GpC accessibility axis. Thus a CpG-unmethylated, unprotected region can acquire GpC methylation.

Readout resolution depends on available GpC sites. CpG/GpC-overlap contexts such as GCG cannot uniquely distinguish native from enzyme-added methylation; the primary implementation separates sequence contexts for interpretation.
The primary paper reports M.CviPI off-target activity affecting CCG-context endogenous methylation at highly accessible regions; the two channels are not perfectly chemically independent.

That citation is assessed as unresolved secondary bibliography because no corresponding primary/metadata source is supplied; it is not used as a method-implementation or origin claim.
